# Notepatra

> Native C++/Rust code editor for the AI era. A fast, lightweight Notepad++-class editor for Linux, macOS, and Windows with local-first AI assistance. Free forever, GPL-3.0, no telemetry in the current release.

Key facts:

- Native Qt5 + QScintilla C++17 application with a Rust core (file I/O, search, diff, formatters) — not Electron; ~14 MB bare binary.
- Syntax highlighting: 82 language lexers covering 238 file extensions, with Light, Dark, and Monokai themes.
- Robust encoding support: UTF-8/16/32 with BOM detection and round-trip, plus heuristics for BOM-less UTF-16 (PowerShell / SQL Server exports).
- Rust-powered search and replace, project-wide search, and a ComparePlus-style side-by-side file compare with word-level diff.
- AI assistance is local-first: works with Ollama, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, OpenAI, and Azure OpenAI. Cloud is optional; nothing leaves the machine unless a cloud backend is explicitly configured.
- Data-analyst tools: CSV analysis, SQLite queries and SQL formatting in every build, plus the DuckDB engine in the Full edition; native charts everywhere, Vega-Lite charts in Full on Linux/Windows. SQL the AI runs is read-only and cannot read local files unless the user approves that query.
- Preview pane (View > Preview Pane, Ctrl+Shift+V): live Markdown, HTML and Jupyter notebook preview beside the editor, and .sql files as runnable SQL cells split by `-- %%` lines. The HTML preview loads nothing from the network.
- Noter: a built-in text-only meeting-notes tool with templates, checklists, note-bound reminders, and PDF/Markdown export.
- Password Generator: a built-in, fully offline generator with three pages on a left rail — random characters, a passphrase drawn from a compiled-in 2,048-word list, and an OpenSSH key pair (Ed25519, ECDSA P-256/P-384, RSA 3072/4096/2048) with an optional aes256-ctr + bcrypt-pbkdf passphrase, a SHA256 fingerprint, and a save that sets 0600 before writing and refuses to overwrite. The key comment is empty by default rather than ssh-keygen's user@host. Its strength readout is the real log2 count of how many values the current settings can produce rather than a heuristic score, and every draw comes from the OS random source (getrandom) via the Rust core.
- Editions: Lite (the complete editor, AI, Data Analyst on CSV + SQLite) and Full (adds DuckDB, plus WebEngine charts and HTML preview on Linux/Windows); features like font packs are downloaded on demand to keep the base binary small.
- Large-file friendly: opens multi-hundred-MB files with automatic safeguards.

## MCP (since v0.1.118)

- From v0.1.118 Notepatra ships notepatra-mcp, a stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 Model Context Protocol server (protocol revision 2025-06-18; 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 also accepted) that connects AI assistants to the running editor over a local socket. Windows named-pipe support was added in v0.1.119 but deadlocked on every verb; it works from v0.1.120.
- Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and any spec-compliant stdio MCP client; cloud-only connector surfaces (ChatGPT connectors, claude.ai web connectors) cannot reach a desktop editor.
- Exposes 119 tools in three tiers (v0.1.133 added 70: git stage/commit/branch/checkout/stash/discard/fetch/pull/push with per-hunk staging and conflict resolution, Noter search/rename/trash/reminders/export, allow-listed preferences and the workspace folder, execute_sql and password-free connection management, rest_request, hex_dump, and tab control, line/case/comment/EOL/encoding edits, undo/redo, save all, rename, view and theme, and pure text tools such as hash, diff, brackets, Markdown and password generation): read (46: tabs, selection, status, search, Noter notes, reminders and note search, read-only Git status/diff/log/show/branch plus hunks and conflicts, npd validation, diagram source read and Mermaid import, read-only SELECT SQL, saved-connection list/query/tables/describe, language list, capability probe, preferences, JSON/SQL/HTML formatting, bracket check and fix, JSON repair, hash, encode, diff, Markdown conversion, symbol list, password generation, hex dump, .http parsing and cURL conversion), act (22: open file, new tab, activate tab, go to line, select range, set language, read-only lock, bookmarks, fold, view settings, theme, Preview pane, compare tabs, compare with file, open note, open Noter panel, create diagram, open Data Analyst, render chart, Manage Connections, schema browser, test_connection), and write (51: insert/replace/find-and-replace, save/save all, close/reload/rename, undo/redo, line, case, comment, EOL and encoding edits, workspace folder, preferences, clear recent files, Noter create/append/reminders/rename/trash/restore/delete/export, set diagram source, export diagram, export query results, export chart, git stage/unstage/commit/branch/checkout/stash/discard/hunk/conflict/fetch/pull/push, execute_sql, add/update/delete connection, rest_request) — every write requires the user to click Approve on a card inside the editor (120-second auto-deny, no headless bypass). run_query reaches saved PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server/SQLite/DuckDB connections read-only (mutations rejected) that run_sql cannot reach; the chart verbs (render_chart, export_chart) need WebEngine: Full edition on Linux and Windows only (macOS Full has none). find_in_tab and search_project take an optional regex flag. run_sql is SELECT-only. Over a CSV in the open workspace folder (csv_path, table data) it runs in DuckDB in Full (engine sandbox: file materialized in-memory, then enable_external_access=false) and in an in-memory SQLite copy in Lite; with no csv_path it queries an empty in-memory SQLite scratch database. Also publishes open tabs and Noter notes as MCP resources plus 3 prompts.
- Tab addressing (since v0.1.126): list_open_tabs publishes a stable `id` per tab and every verb that names a tab accepts `tab_id`. Prefer it over `tab_index`, which is positional and re-points at a different document when a tab closes. read_tab takes max_bytes and always reports truncated + total_chars.
- Credential safety (since v0.1.126, extended in v0.1.127): open_file, read_tab, find_in_tab and both legs of search_project refuse files matching the credential deny-list (SSH/GPG/AWS key directories, id_rsa anywhere on a path, .env files, *.pem, *.key, *.pfx, *.p12, *.jks, Terraform state). In v0.1.125 that check ran only in the filesystem walk, so asking for a key by name still returned it.
- search_project reports workspace_searched and scope; zero matches is a SUCCESS with an empty results list, not an error. format_json rejects invalid JSON with a parse position rather than silently repairing it (in v0.1.125 it returned `[1,2]` for input `[1,2` with isError:false).
- Running notepatra-mcp WITHOUT --socket serves a built-in mock editor: every result carries a [MOCK DATA] content block and _meta.mock, and initialize reports serverInfo.mock. Treat that data as fabricated, never as the user's real files.
- Network: local by default. notepatra-mcp itself opens no network connections (stdio to the client, a local socket to the editor). Tools that use a saved database connection talk to that database with its stored credentials: run_query, list_tables, describe_table and test_connection without an approval card, export_query_results and execute_sql after approval. rest_request, git_fetch, git_pull and git_push run only after approval.
- [MCP documentation](https://notepatra.org/mcp.html): tool reference, per-client setup, security model, FAQ.

## Downloads

- [Official website and installers](https://notepatra.org/): one-line install scripts for Linux/macOS/Windows and direct downloads.
- [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/singhpratech/notepatra/releases): all signed release artifacts with SHA-256 checksums.
